memory_candidates.content: Avoid per-entry subprocess forking (stat, du, readlink) when a shell script must gather metadata or resolve symlinks over many filesystem entries -- batch instead: ONE `find -printf '%U|%T@|%p\n'` call gathers uid/mtime/path for every entry; ONE `du --files0-from=-` call (fed via `printf '%s\0' "${paths[@]}"`) sizes every candidate at once, consuming output positionally since GNU du preserves input order; ONE `readlink -f <many args>` call resolves many symlink targets at once (a failed argument among many simply produces no output line for it, which is fine when only the SET of resolved targets matters, not positional correspondence). Measured: a leaked-/tmp-fixture reaper pass that forked per-entry cost ~44s against a 1,733-entry real backlog (23s of that inside a naive /proc/*/cwd+fd scan over 604 processes/7,186 fds alone); batching brought the same pass down to ~3s.

This harness auto-backgrounds a plain foreground Bash tool call at a fixed ~180s wall-clock mark REGARDLESS of the Bash tool's own `timeout` parameter being raised to 600000ms -- the documented '120000ms default / 600000ms ceiling, raise the parameter to avoid backgrounding' remedy did not prevent it in this environment. When this happens and the agent needs the PID to resolve the wait via the canonical kill-0 bounded-waiter idiom but did not launch the command with a captured `pid=$!` itself, the PID can be recovered safely (no process-name/argv self-match risk) by matching `/proc/*/fd/1`'s readlink target against the known output-log path: `for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do [ "$(readlink "$p/fd/1" 2>/dev/null)" = "$logfile" ] && echo "${p#/proc/}"; done`.

measure-gate-costs.sh's load guard (default threshold 2.0, 1-minute load average) is a real, load-bearing refusal, not a formality: on a shared desktop host with other concurrent sessions/builds, load can rise from under 1.8 to over 3.8 within the ~10 minutes a single expensive test suite takes to run, contaminating any hand-timed re-measurement taken without checking load throughout (not just before) the run. When this happens mid-phase, the correct response is to close the phase [PARTIAL] with the observed load recorded and defer the artifact regeneration to a later, confirmed-idle invocation -- never raise --load-threshold or accept the contaminated figure, per this repo's own explicit Rollback/Contingency precedent for exactly this scenario.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-deploy.sh standing corpus-size probe
sapience_notes.value: The probe (shells out to script-inventory.sh --size-line on every invocation) cost ~2.4s of a ~3.8-4.1s minimal --only-gate invocation against a real agent-system/extensions/ copy -- roughly 58-60% of a gate-narrowed invocation's total wall time. It is now suppressed on any --only-gate/--max-cost-narrowed invocation (GATES_FILTER non-empty) unless a new --corpus-probe opt-in flag is passed; an unfiltered invocation is byte-identical to before.

sapience_notes.subject: Claude Code harness Bash tool auto-backgrounding threshold
sapience_notes.value: In this environment, a plain foreground Bash call is auto-backgrounded by the harness at a fixed ~180s wall-clock mark, independent of the Bash tool's own `timeout` parameter (observed with the parameter explicitly set to 600000ms, its documented ceiling). The documented remedy of raising that parameter to 600000 did not prevent the auto-backgrounding in practice.

sapience_notes.subject: claude-refresh.sh leaked-/tmp-fixture reaper pass
sapience_notes.value: A sixth, independently-gated pass (run_tmp_fixture_pass) was added to claude-refresh.sh, reclaiming tests/run-all.sh's leaked `/tmp/tmp.*` fixtures (SIGKILL from the `-k` grace-period escalation skips a suite's own EXIT trap). It follows the Claude/Lean passes' FORCE-gated three-mode contract, not the build-waiter pass's age-threshold-only one, because removal is irrecoverable. Default age threshold: TMP_FIXTURE_REAP_MIN=1440 minutes (1 day).

sapience_notes.subject: Naive recursive-meta-suite classification grep
sapience_notes.value: grep -lE '(run-all\.sh|verify-deploy\.sh)' over this repo's core test-suite corpus matches 36 files, but only 14 genuinely re-invoke the orchestration layer as a subject under test (the owner's DELETE/KEEP ruling's actual target). The other 22 are either narrow unit/lint suites using the real script only as plumbing (9), or files that only mention the script name in a comment or a planted fixture string a lint asserts against, never executing it for real (13). A bare occurrence count over-counts the genuine class by roughly 2.6x.

sapience_notes.subject: This repository's suite-population count
sapience_notes.value: There is no single answer to 'how many test suites exist' -- four different, legitimate countings coexist: core source-store test-*.sh (157), all-loaded-extensions source-store (197), this repository's deployed .claude/scripts/tests/ tree (179, or 189 including flat siblings), and script-inventory.sh's own corpus-scan test_suites field (204). Each answers a different question; a bare citation of any one without naming which is not safe.
